clues: Biological and geological processes cooperate here to build barriers rather than merely wear them away.
Calcium carbonate deposited by flowing water forms natural dams in a karst landscape.
The continuing growth of these barriers helps create connected lakes, caves and waterfalls.
Upper and lower groups of lakes lie amid forests that shelter bears and wolves.
Find Croatia’s famous protected lake cascade, where tufa barriers divide a forested chain of blue-green waters.
targetLabel: Plitvice Lakes National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: Water can deposit rock as well as erode it. Calcium-carbonate barriers, often called tufa or travertine in descriptions of this property, help maintain its changing cascade of lakes. The target is the park’s published reference point; individual lakes and waterfalls occupy different positions.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
